definition: Intelligent character recognition (ICR) is a method of extracting handwritten text from images.
details: It is a more sophisticated type of OCR technology that recognizes different handwriting styles and fonts to intelligently interpret data from physical documents. ICR is used to organize paper-based unstructured data by scanning documents, extracting information, and adapting extracted data for database storage. ICR algorithms collaborate with OCR to automate data entry from forms by removing the need for keystrokes. It has a high degree of accuracy and is a dependable method for processing various handwritten media quickly.

explainer.lead: Intelligent character recognition extracts handwritten text from images, handling varied handwriting styles and fonts. It matters because it turns paper-based, unstructured documents into data usable by databases.

tiers.eli5: It is a reader that can make sense of your handwriting, not just neat typed letters, so forms can be filled in by machine instead of by hand.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pair ICR with OCR to automate data entry from scanned forms without keystrokes; a pitfall is relying on it where handwriting styles vary widely enough to hurt accuracy.
tiers.paperLevel: A more sophisticated type of OCR that recognizes different handwriting styles and fonts to interpret data from physical documents; it is described as having a high degree of accuracy and is dependable for processing documents.

explainer.example: A scanned paper form is read by ICR, the handwritten entries are extracted, and the values are stored in a database.
